priceSnapshot.note: Endday closed the handover at 86,482.4. Spot rallied to a fresh session high of 87,283.0 at 04:30 UTC (04:00 UTC candle SETTLED its close at 87,169.8, finally clearing the 86,632.6 continuation gate on a settled basis after three straight sessions of failure), then reversed hard: the 05:00 UTC candle closed back at 86,509.0, below the gate again, and a long-liquidation cascade discharged 55,802,365 USD of long liquidations (versus just 255,745 USD of shorts, a roughly 218-to-1 skew) between 06:03 and 07:02 UTC as price fell to 86,277.7 before steadying at 86,393.2 now. Net effect since endday: +139.9 points (+0.16%), but the path was a fire-then-fail of the add gate followed by a sharp long flush - momentum, not direction, is what changed.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below 85,325.2, unchanged for a fifth consecutive report. Tonight's cascade low was 86,277.7 (fills) / 86,175.9 (candle low at 01:00 UTC) - still just over 900 points clear. Not remotely threatened.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close back above 86,632.6. This exact gate DID fire tonight - the 04:00 UTC candle settled its close at 87,169.8, 537.2 points clear - the first settled breach in four sessions. It did not hold: the very next hour closed back under it at 86,509.0 and a $55.8M long-liquidation flush followed. Treat the level as reclaimed-then-lost, not invalidated - it needs a fresh settled close above it, ideally with the liquidation cascade behind rather than ahead of price, before adding further size.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from endday's TAKE_PROFIT (a small defensive trim) to a small ADD, but this is a deliberate small DCA tranche into a flush, not a reaction to the gate firing. Three facts drive the sizing and the timing rather than blocking the trade entirely. FIRST, the add gate that has held for three-plus sessions DID fire on a settled 1H close (87,169.8 at 04:00 UTC, 537.2 points clear of 86,632.6) - real structural confirmation, the kind this desk's own lesson says is allowed to trigger action. SECOND, it reversed within one hour and a 55,802,365 USD long-liquidation cascade (98 fills, 218-to-1 versus shorts) took price to 86,277.7 - a flush of over-levered longs, not fresh aggressive shorting, since open interest fell 0.33% (2,630,402,092 to 2,621,682,444 USD) alongside the drop rather than rising, and the L/S account ratio stayed net-short at 0.96, essentially unchanged from endday's 0.94, meaning the retail base that was already positioned short did not flip long into the rally and is not the source of the flush. THIRD, funding is still pinned at the floor (0.0000231), so there is no leverage cost punishing longs structurally. Per this desk's standing lesson to grade the class of evidence: a settled-close gate fire is structural and earns a real response, but firing-then-failing within an hour, into a fresh RSI extreme (4H 72.58, daily 72.22, both in the 'sizing input, not trigger' zone per the crypto-specific >75-caution rule), argues for a small tranche rather than the full remaining seeder allocation. This session buys 15 USDT of spot at 86,393.2, leaving roughly 19.5 USDT in cash for a second tranche if the flush extends toward the 85,325.2 to 85,111.1 zone, or for the gate's next genuine settled reclaim. Reduce and invalidation levels are unchanged and untested; the add gate is technically the same level but is now explicitly framed as reclaimed-then-lost rather than pristine.

10,331,852.79 USD, entirely long liquidations, across 34 fills - the tail end of the same cascade as it reached its 86,277.7 low. Also already discharged.

liquidityMagnet.note: Called down rather than balanced because the realized data this run is one-sided and recent: 55.8M USD of long liquidations against 0.26M of shorts, all within the last hour, with no verified short-liquidation magnet identified above spot. That said, the L/S account ratio staying net-short at 0.96 through the entire rally and flush means the accounts most exposed to a future squeeze (shorts) were not the ones just flushed - so the immediate pull is down (fresh long liquidity was just proven thin here), but the medium-term short-squeeze setup that has persisted all week is still intact underneath it.

timeframes.structure: Sharp pullback candle: price broke below EMA20 and EMA50 as the liquidation cascade ran, now sitting between EMA100 (86,221.76) and EMA50 (86,504.17), still above EMA200 (85,379.84).

Price (86,393.3) is back above EMA20 (86,349.5) after wicking below it during the flush, and remains well above EMA50/100/200 - trend structure intact, momentum negative and fading from the 71.04 RSI peak set at the 87,169.8 close.

Price holds well above every EMA; MACD histogram has now collapsed six readings in a row (289.64, 252.28, 186.48, 120.28, 88.53, 27.58) and is one print from crossing negative even though RSI is still hot at 72.58 - the same momentum-before-price decay pattern flagged at endday, now more advanced.

Price far above every EMA (EMA20 at 80,218.68 is over 6,000 points below spot); daily MACD histogram still expanding (649.98) and RSI hot at 72.22 - the primary trend is unambiguously up and has not been dented by tonight's intraday flush.
